chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Groups of people come to me and want to hear your hadiths from me, and I become wearied and am not able (to continue).
He said: Then read to them one hadith from its beginning, one hadith from its middle, and one hadith from its end.

key_terms.أَقْوَى: I am able/have strength — indicating the narrator's diminished capacity to continue
key_terms.حَدِيثَكُمْ: Your hadiths — the narrations attributed to the Imam (AS) that his companions were tasked with memorizing and transmitting
key_terms.فَأَضْجَرُ: I become wearied/bored — expressing the emotional and physical toll of repeated narration to many visitors

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq advise his companions to handle the fatigue of transmitting hadiths?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Sinan, a trusted companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), expressed to the Imam his fatigue from the many visitors who came to hear the Imam's hadiths. The Imam's practical remedy was to select hadiths from different parts of the collection — beginning, middle, and end — rather than attempting to recount them all. This guidance reflects the Imam's understanding of the human limits of his companions who served as transmitters of religious knowledge, and his practical method for sustaining hadith transmission without overburdening the narrator.
